messages:
maria: heads-up — escalation from ACME. They removed an Okta group but users stayed active in Redwood. They say SCIM PATCH returned 200 but users still have roles and active=true in our console. They suspect email aliases (user@acme.com vs user+contractor@acme.com) causing mismatch.

alex_admin: yep, started after we switched to alias-based emails. pasted the SCIM request/response we captured: 
```
PATCH /Groups/00d12345
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{
    "op": "remove",
    "path": "members[value eq "user+contractor@acme.com"]"
  }]
}
```
Response 200, body empty. In our admin UI the user is still in role `contractor`.

maria: they also mentioned Okta is sending `value` as the email alias (not externalId). Our SCIM mapping docs say we match `members.value` to `user.externalId` or `primaryEmail` — not against the `emails` array. So likely mismatch.

ozzy: I dug into the logs — Okta patch removed member with value=user+contractor@acme.com. Our membership removal flow resolves users by trying: external_id -> primary_email -> username. We do not iterate the `emails` list or normalize aliases. That explains why removal returned 200 (group mutated) but user lookup failed, so role unlink didn't run.

ryan: can you paste the user object we have? need to confirm `emails[]` contains the alias. Also what does the SCIM change event look like (we ingest group change then schedule membership reconciliation).

alex_admin: here's the user from our API: 
```
GET /Users/urn:uuid:84a1
{
  "userName": "user@acme.com",
  "emails": [{"value": "user@acme.com", "primary": true}, {"value": "user+contractor@acme.com"}],
  "externalId": null,
  "active": true
}
```
SCIM group op used the alias value.

ozzy: confirmed. Proposed immediate workaround: customer can remove the user from the role via Admin console or provide us with the user's `id` in the PATCH (preferred). Medium-term fix: update membership resolver to match `members.value` against the full `emails` array (case-insensitive) and strip common alias tags (plus addressing) if configured for tenant. I'll open a GH PR with tests for: (1) matching emails[] elements, (2) lowercasing, (3) optional alias normalization.

maria: do we have a temporary support playbook entry? customer is a paying ACME account, wants action today.

ozzy: yes — manual steps: 1) admin console -> open user -> remove role; or 2) call our internal admin API: `POST /internal/admin/users/{id}/roles/remove` with role id. I can do a one-off for them if you want.

alex_admin: would appreciate one-off. We can't change Okta right away.

maria: ozzy can you run the manual removal and DM me confirmation? I'll escalate to P2 and attach logs to the ticket.

ozzy: done — removed role for 3 users, confirmed via API. Sent result to ACME via support ticket. Also opened GH issue and draft PR: r/identity#482 — targeting next patch release. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued — PR r/identity#482 will be included in patch-2024.11.1 if approved.

ryan: leaving a note for oncall to watch reconciliation jobs for regressions this week.

maria: thanks team. I'll update the customer and close the escalation after the patch lands and we verify automated removals on next Okta change.
